newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque leaders urge ETA rebels to declare truce.
newsitem.headline: Basque leaders urge ETA rebels to declare truce.

text.p: Spain's northern Basque government called on ETA guerrillas to follow the example of the Irish Republican Army and declare a truce on Saturday, a week after the Basque separatist group killed a young Spanish politician.
Basque leaders made the appeal to ETA in an official declaration issued shortly after the IRA announced a new truce to take effect in Northern Ireland at mid-day on Sunday.

Basque regional Interior Minister Juan Maria Atutxa said an "indefinite truce" by ETA would allow "progress on the road to peace". "The public outcry of the past week points precisely in that direction," he said.
Millions of Spaniards have taken to the streets to vent their outrage against ETA for the killing last weekend of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, a Basque town councillor.
Atutxa said ETA was now faced with "an historic moment and a chance to give a future of peace and hope to this people ... There is no doubt that the future is in their hands."
Atutxa urged ETA's political arm, Herri Batasuna, to support the call for a truce just as the IRA's political arm Sinn Fein had backed such a move by the rebels in Northern Ireland.
"Every day that passes without a condemnation of ETA's crimes and without support for a truce makes (Herri Batasuna) more of an accomplice to the murders committed," he said.
A spokesman for Herri Batasuna declined comment.
ETA has killed nearly 800 people in its struggle for an independent Basque homeland encompassing parts of northern Spain and southern France.
